Acquisition.com http://Acquisition.com helps businesses scale. We hold data from thousands of client businesses, including company profiles, purchases, product usage, and live connections to bank, CRM, and advertising accounts. Our founders have said the company must be data-first before it can be AI-first. This role makes that true.

We are hiring our first Director of Data, the first leader solely accountable for the data function. Three Senior Data Engineers and a half-time analyst run the warehouse, single-client-record pipelines, and reporting used by Finance and Leadership, supporting two client-facing products in daily use. You report to the CTO; Platform owns infrastructure and application engineering; AI Engineering owns model architecture and runtime; and you own the data those systems train on, evaluate against, and retrieve from.  - Enforce privacy and access controls in the data layer with Security and Legal, including retention, deletion, cataloging, lineage, and boundaries between operating companies and partners.

 - Lead the data team as one program through a published roadmap, clear operating cadence, documented on-call, talent development, and hands-on technical leadership when the work requires it.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

ACS (Allen Control Systems) is a defense technology company building precision robotic systems for the United States and its allies. Founded by two former U.S. Navy electrical engineers with deep experience in robotics and software, ACS brings together AI, computer vision, precision motion, and advanced hardware to solve complex defense challenges across land, air, and maritime environments.

ABOUT BUILD AI

Build AI is the data hyperscaler for Physical AI. We're vertically integrated across hardware, manufacturing, logistics, collection, and model training to scale the physical labor dataset orders of magnitude faster than anyone in the world.


JOB SUMMARY

We've collected the largest dataset of physical labor in the world. We're scaling to 1B hours over the next two years, collecting data from 100M+ people worldwide. You'll build and lead the team that writes the software to get us there.


HOW DATA COLLECTION WORKS

We give wearable cameras to field teams and partners. Each day, they recruit workers, assign devices, pay workers to wear the cameras on the job, collect the devices/SD cards, and upload the footage. At scale, inefficiency, fraud, and human error emerge: devices and SD cards get lost or stolen, devices sit idle, and contributors produce poor-quality data.


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Build the team: hire and lead the Shenzhen software team. You set the hiring bar, the technical direction, and the pace, and you stay hands-on while the team grows.

 - Vendor platform: the Android and web app that coordinates our operators, partners, and vendors as they source, onboard, and pay contributors and businesses. That covers device assignment, attendance, collection tracking, payments, and fraud/loss prevention. Like Didi or Uber, but for data collection.

 - Partner growth: referral programs that grow the partner network, and models that forecast how much data existing and new partners can collect.

 - Data infrastructure: upload, storage, and processing pipelines that run at petabytes per month and grow 10× a year.

 - Data QA: orchestrate, train, and fine-tune models for a QA pipeline that catches bad data automatically.

 - Recruiting tools: software that speeds up hiring across the company.

 - Anything else that is blocking scale.

You'll work directly with the founders and the global ops team, and you'll own outcomes end to end, from setting priorities to shipping and supporting the work.


CULTURE FIT

 - You believe your life is wasted if you do not change the world in some non-trivial way.

 - You are excited to put everything into the company to do your life's work.

 - You love solving hard problems. The harder, the better.

 - You thrive with autonomy: spot problems, solve them, own the outcome.


REQUIREMENTS

 - Have built and led an engineering team, including hiring strong engineers yourself.

 - Have built and shipped software that real users depend on, and are still hands-on.

 - Comfortable across frontend, backend, APIs, and databases.

 - Fluent in English and able to be based in Shenzhen full time.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Android app development.

 - Data pipelines, large file uploads, or ML/QA systems.

 - Hiring experience in Shenzhen.

 - Can start immediately.


BENEFITS

 - Competitive pay

 - Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage

 - $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefit

Overjet is the world-leader in dental AI. Already, thousands of dental providers and insurers rely on our platform to deliver the best possible care. Now, we’re looking for talented people to fulfill our mission: improve oral health for all.

Overjet is where builders become leaders. Everyone here loves to make new things: new products, new partnerships, new content, and a new category of AI technology. And as Overjet grows ridiculously fast, so will you.

Simply put, there’s no better place to accelerate your career. Come join us!




THE MISSION AND THE HARD PART

Dentistry is a MANY BILLION DOLLAR industry whose marketing all looks the same. Stock smiles, blue gradients, a dentist pointing at an X-ray. The people we need to reach, dental practice owners and Dental Service Organziation executives, have learned to scroll past it in under a second. We want you to make the first dental content they stop for.

You'll help set the creative vision for everything that carries Overjet's name: the look, the voice, the bar. Then you'll make the flagship work yourself, script to storyboard to final cut, directing AI video in Runway, Higgsfield, and whatever ships next. You've originated and shipped creative that performed, not just executed someone else's concept, ideally somewhere you built the process as you went. 6+ years in creative production or direction, 2+ directing other creators, a portfolio of finished AI video. You give feedback that makes other people's work better. You don't need to know dentistry. You need to be willing to study an audience until you can predict what it watches. We don't have the usual dysfunction that plagues fast-growing companies. Now we're at an interesting inflection point. We need to double the engineering organization while keeping everything that made us fast. That's the core problem: how do you stay fast and maintain code quality and culture while you scale from 40 to 80+ engineers?

The best engineering organizations don't scale because they hire more of the right people. They scale because they've designed how decisions get made, how work gets prioritized, how teams coordinate without creating meetings overhead, how people get unblocked. The operating system is the difference between a team that grows and a team that fractures under its own weight.

Socket has a strong technical leadership team. What we're missing is someone who owns the operating system. Someone who looks at how we're currently shipping things and says "this works for 40 people, but it won't work for 80, and here's what we need to change. Someone who understands that keeping engineers happy and keeping the product moving fast are the same problem, not competing problems.

This role is about protecting what we've built while scaling it. It's about designing planning processes and team structure and decision-making rhythms that are lightweight enough to stay fast and rigorous enough that dependencies surface before they become problems. It's about identifying the engineering leaders who can own their domains and then creating the conditions where they can do their best work.

You'll spend about two-thirds of your time on operations and people leadership. The other third stays hands-on technical. Not because we need more code reviewed, but because your technical credibility determines whether people actually trust your leadership on the hard calls.

ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.


About the Role
We are looking for a Head of AI Native Operations to build the autonomous systems that run Supabase.


Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system, where agents carry the operational load end to end. We are standing up a new central team to build that platform and run it in production. This is the role that leads it, and it is hands-on. You design the architecture, build the first versions of the critical pieces, and are accountable for whether every agent we run is correct, safe, and improving over time. We build rather than buy, and there are no settled best practices for most of this yet, so you will be setting them.

You will lead a team of senior individual contributors extending the platform and driving adoption across teams.

What You’ll Be Responsible For
In this role, you’ll:

 - Own the agent platform architecture: The harness and orchestration layer and connectors into company systems, shared context and memory, and the path from prototype to production.

 - Catch regressions before they ship: Model, prompt, and tool changes can’t ship until they pass the evals. When a new model comes out, you know within hours whether to adopt it.

 - Make every agent observable: Every run and every decision is traced. For any agent at any time, you can answer what it did, why, what it cost, and how its quality is trending.

 - Own safety and trust: Design the controls that let agents act without a human in the loop: least-privilege credentials, hard policy limits, escalation thresholds, audit logs, sandboxing, and prompt-injection defenses.

 - Replace workflows, don’t assist them: Pick the workflows agents can fully own today and take them to production.

 - Turn wins into a platform: Package what works into reusable components, templates, and eval harnesses so other teams can ship their own production agents without starting from scratch.

 - Build and direct the team: Hire and grow senior ICs, review their designs and pull requests, and hold the quality bar.

 - Measure what matters: Track workflows automated, eval pass rates, cost per run, and work absorbed against the hiring plan.



How You’ll Think


A Point of View on Where Automation Wins
You have a thesis about how AI and automation change the way a company operates, and it comes from building, not reading. You can look at a business and say which workflows agents can own today, which they will own in 12 months as models improve, and which still need people, and why. You defend that view with evidence from systems you have shipped, and you update it when the evals tell you to.


Eval-Driven
You don’t trust an agent because the demo looked good. You trust it because it passes a test set

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

**About the role**
------------------

The Director, Production Analytics owns Production Analytics globally: every site, every product line, and every production function across Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, Supply Chain, Planning, and Warehousing / Material Management. The ambition is not better dashboards. It is that a division leader can tell whether they will hit rate before they miss it, and that when we argue about where to invest, the argument is settled by data rather than by whoever presents best.

### **ABOUT THE JOB**

This is a player-coach role. You will lead the hardest analytical problems yourself, on the programs that matter most to the company, and build a team that can run several more in parallel. You will be judged on what you accomplish, not on how you operate: whether a program hit rate that would otherwise have slipped, whether a constraint got cleared because we saw it coming, whether a number leadership used to make a real decision came from this team.  
We weigh approach over domain familiarity. The strongest analytics leaders we have are exceptional at how they attack a problem, even where they arrived without the functional background. Manufacturing depth is useful and listed below as preferred, but it does not substitute for analytical method, judgment about what matters, and the ability to drive a result through an organization.

**What you'll do**
------------------

Pedestal Health (formerly Target RWE) is a rapidly growing company at the intersection of clinical research, healthcare, and technology, focused on reimagining clinical evidence generation. The company partners with pharmaceutical and biotech companies, providers, and payers to generate rigorous, multimodal evidence that supports clinical, regulatory, and strategic decision-making across the full lifecycle of care. As trials and real-world data blend into continuous evidence generation, this mosaic is becoming the field's central problem.

Pedestal Health is hiring a Head of Technology to build the foundation that makes the mosaic trustworthy. You will lead data engineering, cloud infrastructure, our internal data and application platforms, and corporate IT and security through a team of engineering and IT leaders. Phykion is reimagining aviation fuel. We cultivate hyper-productive microalgae to produce a scalable, low-carbon oil that drops directly into the HEFA pathway — the most commercially established route to sustainable aviation fuel. Our platform is built on three breakthroughs: a field-proven algae host with 5+ years of outdoor cultivation, strain engineering trait stacking that has delivered a 10x gain in oil productivity to date, and an outdoor cultivation process on non-arable land fed by seawater and CO2. About the Role

Abnormal AI protects organizations from the most sophisticated email and collaboration attacks using behavioral AI. Security is not a bolt-on at Abnormal; it is core to the product we sell and the trust our customers place in us. Our security organization operates a commercial cloud environment and a separate FedRAMP-authorized environment, and we are pursuing increasingly rigorous federal authorizations as we grow.

We are hiring a Director of Security reporting to the CISO and leading the Security Engineering organization. You will build and scale high-performing security teams, own major security programs end to end, and operate autonomously in the CISO's absence, including representing security to executive leadership, customers, and auditors.

You have built security teams from the ground up, you write and review code and architecture when it matters, and you believe the best security organizations earn their influence through partnership rather than policy enforcement.

Our Security Philosophy

We run security the way the best engineering-led companies do:
- Security reduces toil. Our job is to make the rest of the company faster and safer at the same time. If a control adds friction without reducing risk, it is a defect.
- Paved paths, safe by default. We invest in guardrails, golden paths, and secure-by-default infrastructure so the easy choice is the secure choice. We prefer preventing classes of problems over chasing individual findings.
- Partnership over gatekeeping. Security succeeds only through deep collaboration with engineering, IT, and business teams. We embed with builders, we ship alongside them, and we take on their constraints as our own.
- Engineering-grade rigor. We treat security problems as engineering problems: automated, measurable, code-reviewed, and continuously improved.

If the security cultures that value freedom and responsibility, context over control, and guardrails over gates resonate with you, you will feel at home here.

- Serve as deputy to the CISO: act with full authority in the CISO's absence and represent the security organization to executives, customers, and regulators.
- Lead, coach, and grow managers and senior engineers across Security Engineering and Security Operations.
- Own the security engineering roadmap: cloud security architecture (AWS-first), detection and response, identity, vulnerability management, and secure-by-default platform investments.
- Drive cross-functional programs with Engineering, IT, and Product, from AI security governance to data perimeter controls to federal compliance initiatives.
- Set and defend engineering standards for the security organization: everything as code, automated where possible, measured against outcomes rather than activity.

About Alta

Alta Resource Technologies (Alta) is a next generation mining company that uses synthetic biology to separate critical minerals from conventional and unconventional resources, including e-waste. Founded in 2023, the company is expanding its team in Boulder, CO. The exponential growth of new tech industries, as well as the information technology sector, are driving historic growth in mineral demand and stressing existing supply streams. Meeting new demand, diversifying the supply chain, and producing minerals in a more sustainable manner requires the rapid development, deployment and scaling of new technologies. This mineral challenge represents a historic opportunity for technology development and value creation. Alta is proud to be at the vanguard of this mega trend.

Alta is reinventing how the world sources critical minerals — using protein-based chemistry to extract rare earth elements and other essential materials from challenging feedstocks with unmatched selectivity. As global demand accelerates, securing these materials has become one of the most urgent challenges facing U.S. competitiveness and national security. The ideal candidate is a proven builder of teams and a hands-on expert in industrial fermentation of Bacillus and other microbial systems. You will translate bench-scale results into robust, transferable processes, represent Alta's bioprocess capabilities to partners, investors, and government stakeholders, and serve as a key member of the technical leadership team.

About Carrot:

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com .

The Opportunity  🚀

Carrot is looking for a Director, Information Security to lead the security program that protects the highly sensitive fertility and family-building data of members around the world. You will set the security strategy, own both corporate security (GRC, incident response, security awareness, vendor risk) and product security (application, cloud and infrastructure security, secure development lifecycle), and serve as the trusted voice on Carrot's security posture with executives, auditors, and enterprise customers.

Day to day, you will balance setting direction with staying close to the work: prioritizing risk with Engineering and IT, guiding audit and certification cycles, coaching a small and talented team, and joining customer conversations where security is part of the buying decision. Carrot has already earned SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS compliance, so this role is about taking a strong foundation to the next level of maturity, not starting from scratch.

What makes this role different is the combination of stakes and influence. Few security leaders get to protect data this personal, at global scale, while working directly with executive leadership and shaping how a health platform is built, sold, and trusted.

What You’ll Own 💼

In this role, you will:
- Lead Carrot's security strategy and roadmap, using a recognized maturity model (such as C2M2 or NIST CSF) to prioritize investments and report progress to executive leadership
- Own the full security program across corporate security (GRC, incident management, security awareness, third-party risk) and product security (application security, cloud and infrastructure security, secure SDLC)
- Partner with Engineering, especially the Internal Platform team, to build security into how Carrot designs, ships, and operates its systems, going beyond compliance
- Lead internal risk assessment

Who we are

DigiCert is a global leader in intelligent trust. We protect the digital world by ensuring the security, privacy, and authenticity of every interaction. Our AI-powered DigiCert ONE platform unifies PKI, DNS, and certificate lifecycle management, to secure infrastructure, software, devices, messages, AI content and agents. Learn why more than 100,000 organizations, including 90% of the Fortune 500, choose DigiCert to stop today’s threats and prepare for a quantum-safe future at  www.digicert.com

Job summary

AI agents are moving from experimentation into production—accessing enterprise data, invoking tools, writing code, and acting on behalf of people and organizations. As they become more autonomous, enterprises need a new trust layer: one that establishes who an agent is, who owns it, what it is authorized to do, and how that authority can be revoked. GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

General Description

The systems our OT clients run treat drinking water, move natural gas, run production lines, and keep hospital equipment working. Many were installed before anyone thought about attackers, and plenty still run software the vendor stopped supporting years ago. You can't take a refinery controller offline on a Tuesday afternoon to patch it, and you can't reboot a substation to check whether a fix worked. This work needs people who understand the physical process as well as the network, and we've built a team of them. When we do it well, nobody outside the plant ever hears about it. GuidePoint Security is hiring a Director, OT/IoT Security Services to lead that team.

You'll report to the SVP of Offensive Security and own the practice: the team, the service catalog, delivery quality, and the P&L. The delivery managers already run day-to-day projects well, so expect to spend most of your time with engineers and clients, and to be the senior escalation point when a technical or client issue gets complicated. The rest goes to supporting regional sales teams, other GuidePoint Security practices, and technology partners.

In this practice, "Wow Them" means an account executive gets a scope and price back quickly, our engineers work safely on a running plant floor, and the client calls us for their next site.

About the OT/IoT Security Services Practice

The OT/IoT Security Services practice protects the industrial systems our clients depend on in energy, water, manufacturing, healthcare, transportation, and other critical infrastructure sectors. We deliver in every GuidePoint Security region and provide the services behind GuidePoint Security's OT technology partnerships.

Most of the team came to security from the plant floor or the military: veterans and former engineers from utilities, oil and gas, manufacturing, and nuclear power. They know what an operator is thinking when a consultant walks into the control room with a laptop, and safety and uptime come first on every job.

A typical client relationship starts with finding out what's actually on the OT network and where it's exposed. From there we design segmentation and controls that don't interrupt operations, and many clients stay with us for ongoing OT vulnerability management. The Opportunity:

A heat pump is a fifteen-year relationship with a homeowner, and the second year matters as much as the first week. This role owns whether Jetson's systems keep working — and how fast we respond when they don't.

As Director of Technical Service, you lead Jetson's service organization and act as the company's senior technical authority in the field. You own callback rate, first-time fix rate, and time to resolution. You own warranty administration and the money we recover from manufacturers, customers and CARE programs. This is a build-and-run role: you'll be designing the service function while operating it, across multiple markets at once.

- Own service capacity, dispatch, and on-call coverage, including surge planning for heating and cooling season peaks
- Own warranty administration and manufacturer claims, and recover cost wherever warranty applies

- Partner with Director of Customer Success and Director of Production Coordination  on service recovery, escalation handling, and customer communication during outages
- Partner with Supply Chain on service parts strategy, truck stock, and warranty inventory
- Serve as final technical escalation authority, including safety, code compliance, and refrigerant handling issues
- Report weekly to leadership on callbacks, first-time fix, open service aging, and warranty recovery, with root cause and a plan attached to each

Muon seeks a Senior Director of EO/IR Instrument Engineering to lead the strategy, development, and delivery of our electro-optical and infrared instrument portfolio, from system architecture through on-orbit calibration. In this role, you will build, mentor, and guide a multidisciplinary engineering organization that is roughly doubling in size, while establishing the technical direction and operational rigor needed to scale across a growing portfolio of flight programs. As a senior technical and organizational leader, you will own instrument performance, cost, schedule, and overall business outcomes, ensuring alignment between engineering execution and mission objectives. Reporting to the SVP of Mission Execution, you will serve on the Mission Execution leadership team, shaping Muon’s EO/IR strategy, developing organizational capabilities, and driving the successful execution of our instrument portfolio.

- Set EO/IR strategy for the company

- Own the multi-year investment plan for instrument technology, lab and test infrastructure, and the organization's operating budget.

Pelago is the leading specialty substance use care provider, built on the belief that effective treatment means matching care intensity to what each member actually needs rather than defaulting to the most expensive intervention. Our programs guide members through every stage of the substance use spectrum, from unhealthy habits to active use disorders, delivering personalized treatment for tobacco, alcohol, opioid, cannabis, and stimulant use based on individual health, habits, genetics, and goals.

With Sona, our voice-first AI Mental Health Specialist, Pelago now applies that same clinically-driven model to mental health, pairing deep clinical expertise with technology to expand access without compromising care quality. We believe technology should make clinical care more precise and more human, not replace the judgment behind it.

Pelago has scaled to helping hundreds of employers and health plans and has already helped more than 750,000 members better manage their substance use. If you're passionate about AI and making an impact on the health of others, join us and make it happen!

Our engineering team operates as empowered, outcome-oriented problem solvers, working in close partnership with product, design, and clinical teams to improve member outcomes at scale.

- Shape how we work—our tools, processes, and culture

sitemap:at&t:102055599776.description:
This is a full-time onsite role based in the location(s) posted and is performed from the designated work location five days per week. No relocation is offered.

AT&T's Chief Security Office is seeking an experienced cybersecurity leader to direct the strategy, architecture, governance, and operational effectiveness of the company's enterprise network security program. This position is accountable for the design, governance, and continuous improvement of enterprise firewall architecture, network segmentation strategy, intrusion detection and prevention capabilities (IDS/IPS), and other critical security controls that protect AT&T's infrastructure, applications, data, and services.

The Director leads multiple cybersecurity functions responsible for enterprise firewall governance, security architecture, segmentation programs, perimeter defense, threat detection and prevention, compliance, security engineering, and modernization initiatives. This role partners across technology and business organizations to reduce cyber risk, improve operational efficiency, and enable secure business transformation.

Key Responsibilities and Required Qualifications
- Leads enterprise firewall strategy, architecture, lifecycle management, governance, policy standards, rule management, and access controls.
- Modernizes firewall platforms through simplification, automation, scalability, compliance, technical debt reduction, and attack-surface minimization.
- Defines enterprise network segmentation and micro-segmentation strategies that protect critical assets and reduce lateral movement.
- Develops long-term network security architecture roadmaps with infrastructure, cloud, and application teams, balancing risk reduction and business enablement.
- Provides executive leadership for IDS/IPS, detection engineering, threat prevention, monitoring, analytics, continuous tuning, and incident readiness.
- Advances scalable security engineering through automation, orchestration, analytics, AI-enabled capabilities, policy automation, and workflow optimization.
- Establishes governance, audit readiness, executive metrics, dashboards, objectives, and performance indicators that demonstrate measurable risk reduction.
- Leads and develop high-performing cybersecurity teams, set priorities, build future leaders, and influence executive investment and risk decisions.
- Brings 10+ years of cybersecurity or network security experience, including 5+ years leading enterprise-scale programs or engineering teams in complex, regulated environments.
- Demonstrates deep expertise in enterprise firewalls, network segmentation, IDS/IPS, access governance, network and cloud security architecture, threat modeling, secure design, monitoring, and cybersecurity frameworks.

Education/Experience:
- Master's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or related field with 10+ years of related experience.

Preferred Qualifications
- CISSP, CISM, CCSP, GIAC, or equivale

sitemap:citi (jobs.citi.com):10216104211.description:
Citi's COO Technology organization is building one of the most consequential AI platforms in global financial services — and this is the role that leads it.

The Head of AI Solutions is a newly created, executive-level position with a clear mandate: architect a unified AI strategy, build a world-class engineering team, and deliver production-grade AI at scale across the operational nerve center of a global bank. This is not a coordination or advisory role. It is a builder's role — one with the budget, the mandate, and the organizational reach to make it real.

You will own the AI strategy and delivery capability across a $200M+ technology portfolio spanning some of the most operationally complex domains in banking: KYC, fraud detection, wholesale lending operations, global reconciliations, cash management, payments control, non-financial regulatory reporting, payroll, and international operations . The scale is significant, the problems are highly complex at this stage, and the impact is direct — the solutions you build will influence how trillions of dollars in transactions flow daily, how regulatory risk is managed, and how Citi's operational infrastructure evolves over the next decade.

Unlike a role at a pure-play technology company, you will be solving AI challenges where failure has regulatory and systemic consequence — and where success reshapes the economics and resilience of critical global operations. The ambiguity is real, the stakes are high, and the opportunity for lasting impact is unmatched.

This role reports directly to the Head of COO Technology.

Responsibilities:

AI Strategy & Platform Architecture:
- Define and own the multi-year AI strategy for the COO Technology portfolio; translate business intent into a concrete, milestone-driven execution roadmap with measurable outcomes
- Develop architecture blueprints and end-to-end systems design for Generative AI and agentic workflows across diverse operational domains
- Build the shared AI platform — reusable models, tooling, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and accelerators — that reduces duplication, lowers cost, and enables faster adoption across COO
- Establish and enforce engineering standards, architectural guardrails, and development patterns across all AI initiatives
- Define a rigorous total cost of ownership model for developing, deploying, and sustaining AI in production
- Identify and evaluate emerging GenAI technologies, foundation models, and agent frameworks — and make deliberate, defensible decisions on where to build, buy, or partner

Production AI Delivery at Enterprise Scale
- Lead end-to-end delivery of AI solutions across high-complexity, regulated operational environments — from architecture through production deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement
- Drive the agentic product development lifecycle: runtime harness design, evaluation frameworks, human-in-the-loop workflows, feedback loops, and production readiness criteria
- Manage cross-function

The Commercial Payments division within Optum Financial operates as a payment service provider (PSP) that enables healthcare, property & casualty, and warranty payers to efficiently distribute claim payments to providers through a centralized, multi-rail platform. By accepting payment instructions via file or API, the division orchestrates end-to-end payment delivery across multiple modalities-including ACH, ACH+, virtual credit cards, and checks-aligned to provider payment preferences. Increasingly, the division is evolving beyond a facilitation model to offer flexible service configurations, including full-service options with fund custody and compliance management, positioning Optum Financial to address diverse payer needs and capture broader market opportunities.

Optum Financial is seeking a strategic and technically fluent Senior Director, Payments Platform to lead the vision, development, and modernization of Payments 2.0 and CCS 2.0. This leader will define and deliver a scalable, AI-native, API-first platform that powers end-to-end healthcare payment and communications experiences across payers, providers, internal operations, and strategic partners. As Commercial Payments transitions from legacy point solutions to a unified platform model, this role will be instrumental in advancing the Optum Payments Network strategy.

The ideal candidate brings deep payments and fintech platform expertise, solid product management discipline, and proven 0-to-1 platform leadership. They will lead cross-functional teams across Product, Engineering, Architecture, AI, Operations, Security, Compliance, and Commercial functions to build scalable, secure, and commercially viable platform capabilities spanning payment orchestration, onboarding, fulfillment, communications, APIs, transaction visibility, and enterprise-scale operations.

We're living through a once-in-a-generation shift in how work gets done. Data, automation, and AI are quickly becoming the center of every business decision - and Alteryx is leading the transformation.

Alteryx is the agentic analytics and automation company that powers actionable insights for more than 8,000 customers worldwide — organizations that together run over 380 million automated workflows a year on the Alteryx platform. Citi is looking for a Senior Manager, AI Risk and Controls to lead independent oversight of AI use cases and AI assets across the business, ensuring every deployment meets Citi's governance standards and applicable regulatory requirements. Sitting within Citi's Non-Financial Risk function, this is a high-impact leadership role that places you at the centre of one of the most strategically important challenges in financial services — governing AI responsibly at scale. At Cloudera, we empower people to transform complex data into clear and actionable insights. - Cross-Functional Influence: Collaborate closely with Sales, Product Management, Engineering, and Marketing to ensure Cloudera’s AI solutions align with evolving market dynamics and customer pain points.

Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. Work like this is worth far more solved once, well, and for everyone than solved separately on six teams.

We are forming a centralized Data Platform Enablement team to own that category of work, and we are hiring its founding engineering leader.

The Data Domain Owner will own and lead the strategic direction, prioritization, and governance for one of DaVita’s five enterprise data domains (Village). workday:first management:JR17266.description:
This job combines two things that usually sit with different people: owning products and building them. One product is a real-time tracking and communications app that hundreds of thousands of families and their school districts rely on, where a wrong notification reaches a parent waiting at a bus stop. The other is the technology behind a service for students with special transportation needs, students experiencing homelessness, and out-of-district students, delivered through contracted local transportation providers.
Each product has a Business Product Owner who owns its business outcomes, priorities, and commercial decisions. You are their partner on the IT side, owning how those priorities become software within the lines our product management operating model sets. It gets built in an agentic delivery framework owned by a senior technical team. You own its product side: the specs, acceptance criteria, and evals that go in, and the call on whether the result met the business need.
You also build. In traditional product management, requirements get written, handed to engineering, and interpreted somewhere along the way. Here, a conversation with a stakeholder can become working software in days, and the person who had the conversation is often the one directing the agents that build it. You should already be building with agents, even if it is not yet how you do all of your work. In this role, building stops being something you do alongside product management and becomes how you do it.
You will start with a small team, so expect to lead and build at the same time. The people you lead may come from more traditional roles, and helping them make the same shift is part of the job. You will also own the budget, vendor relationships, and contracts behind this work, AI tooling included.

How You'll Work
AI runs through your entire workflow, from discovery and specs to the build, tests, documentation, and reporting. We are looking for someone already working this way who can show what it has produced, not someone with a thesis on where AI is going.
Requirements here usually arrive as a conversation rather than a ticket, and you will often be the one having it. You will build inside a framework someone else runs, which means understanding a rule's reasoning before deciding it is in your way. You will be measured on whether what ships is correct and whether the business got what it actually needed, not on volume.

A typical week may include:
- Sitting with district staff, families, or the team that coordinates our transportation providers, then deciding with a Business Product Owner whether a problem belongs on the roadmap.
- Turning a conversation like that into a working prototype and using it to agree on requirements before the full build starts.
- Reviewing work with a team member who is still learning to build with agents, and explaining the reasoning behind your feedback.

Current HHMI Employees, click here to apply via your Workday account.

HHMI is focused on supporting and moving science forward in a variety of different ways ranging from conducting basic biomedical research, empowering educators, inspiring students, developing the next generation of scientists – even stretching into film and media production.  Our Headquarters is in the greater Washington, DC metro area and is home to over 300 employees with expertise in investments , communications, digital production, biomedical sciences, and everything in between.  The work housed here supports and augments the groundbreaking research conducted in HHMI labs across the nation.  As HHMI scientists continue to push boundaries in laboratories and classrooms, you can be sure that your contributions while working here are making a difference.

This is a role for someone who can run a function that cannot fail while rebuilding it at the same time.

HHMI is a nonprofit scientific research organization that supports scientists and educators across the country. Finance and People & Culture run the processes that pay, hire, reimburse, and support all of them. Most of those legacy processes were built for a world before Workday was mature and before AI could do real work. That world is gone. HHMI is moving procurement and expense onto Workday and is putting AI tools in the hands of every employee through EverydayAI. The open question is what the processes themselves should look like, and that is what this role answers.

HHMI’s EverydayAI initiative is putting AI tools and agents into operations across the institute. You will not need to build the business case for AI or convince leadership it matters. That work is done. What you will do is decide where AI belongs in payroll and finance processes, partner with the EverydayAI and Technology teams to build and pilot the first agents and be honest about what works and what does not.

You start with payroll, and you own it. You lead the payroll team and are accountable for every cycle running accurately and on time across the three populations. At the same time, you take the function apart end to end and redesign it: Workday-native, with AI and agents doing the work they are good at and people doing the work that needs judgment. Then you implement it with your team. You do not need to arrive as a payroll expert. You do need to learn the operation, exercise sound judgment, and lead changes that preserve accurate, on-time pay, working with an experienced payroll manager.

Once payroll is running the new way, you carry the same method into the rest of Finance and People & Culture.

These workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for the off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply. That constraint is the job. We’re hiring an engineering leader to build and run Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters : the team responsible for implementing security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA’s hardware engineers design silicon on, spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud environments. You’ll operate as the peer counterpart to NVIDIA’s company-wide security organization and to hardware infrastructure engineering, translating enterprise security intent into controls that hold up at EDA scale without slowing chip design down.

We don’t expect you to arrive fluent in every security product category; we do expect you to own security outcomes from day one and to acquire the remaining domain breadth fast. - Run the full lifecycle of core infrastructure security technologies: selection, deployment, operation, and eventual replacement.

PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

The Stuckeman School in the College of Arts and Architecture at Penn State seeks a responsive, visionary, and thoughtful leader to serve as Head of the Department of Architecture.

The Department of Architecture is grounded in a longstanding culture of interdisciplinary collaboration. Working collaboratively with faculty and administrators across the School and College, the Department Head will identify new opportunities and strategic directions in response to complex institutional, financial, academic, and societal challenges. The successful candidate will demonstrate effective communication, sound judgment, fiscal responsibility, and the ability to make timely, decisive decisions. They will embrace change as an opportunity for innovation while upholding the academic excellence, integrity, and values of the Department, the School, the College, and the University.

The next Department Head will work to implement the Department’s 2026-2030 strategic plans and support strategic goals and initiatives across the School, College, and University. At Pfizer, our business development and strategic planning teams serve as the corporate face in crucial negotiations that influence our capacity to deliver life-changing breakthroughs for patients. We seek passionate colleagues like you who can tackle challenges head-on and innovate groundbreaking solutions to fulfill our mission. Your dedication is essential in navigating complex scenarios and driving forward our commitment to transforming patient lives. Join us in this vital role where your contributions will be pivotal in achieving our goals and making a significant impact on global health.

At Pfizer, our mission is to create breakthroughs that change patients’ lives. As part of the Customer Experience function in the Chief Technologist Organization, we are seeking a Director, AI Experience Design Lead to own how Pfizer’s AI looks, sounds, and behaves, and to build and lead the design team that ships it.

Pfizer is putting AI in front of 80,000 colleagues and every surface needs to feel like it came from the same company. This role owns that consistency as a product: the AI-first design system behind human and agent experiences. It defines what colleagues see, what agents say, how uncertainty gets disclosed, and how regulated content behaves. The deliverables are working systems: tokens, patterns, and standards that live in MCP and flow into the build pipeline, so engineers and the Design QA Agent get the correct pattern by default and teams build compliant experiences without waiting on review cycles.

The Director is accountable for the system the way a product owner is accountable for a product: adoption in code, pattern reuse, override rates, and first-pass compliance are the scoreboard. When telemetry shows a pattern failing, the Director retires it.

This role is designed for a highly experienced design leader who brings exceptional executive presence, narrative storytelling ability, and political acumen, while remaining deeply hands-on and invested in growing the people on their team: a player-coach who ships production design work alongside the team and leads complex, high-stakes design initiatives across Pfizer’s AI platforms and enterprise LLM integrations.

This is a Director-level role combining people leadership with deep individual contribution. The Director works across every modality the platforms speak (screens, conversation, voice, and agent-to-agent interaction) and moves fluidly between shipping production design work, delivering design standards as code, and growing the team. Deep technical understanding of how LLMs, agents, and modern product stacks behave anchors the role’s credibility with Engineering and Product.

Join Pfizer International Commercial Division, Business Transformation organization to leverage cutting-edge technology for critical business decisions and enhance customer experiences for colleagues, patients, and physicians. Our team of data engineering, data science, and AI professionals is at the forefront of Pfizer’s transformation into a digitally driven organization, using data science and AI to change patients’ lives, leading process and engineering innovations to advance AI and data science applications from prototypes and MVPs to full production.

As the AI Data Architect you will be the senior individual-contributor authority for AI-ready data across International Commercial. This role owns the architecture and modelling backbone of the AI data product portfolio: dimensional and semantic model design, AI readiness assessment frameworks, and data product blueprints, from source analysis through to certified, AI-consumable data assets.

·       Extend AI readiness beyond structured data: define architectures and enrichment strategies (parsing, chunking, metadata, embeddings) that make unstructured content such as documents, transcripts and field notes AI-consumable
·       Define reusable standards, blueprints and accelerators that enable market teams to achieve AI readiness independently

The vision for Pfizer’s Digital function is a more integrated and coordinated healthcare model that improves patient outcomes, fuels tomorrow’s breakthrough therapies, and brings medicines to patients faster.

Within Platform Engineering, the Spark Pro team builds and runs Pfizer’s internal developer platform — the paved road that lets any engineering team take an idea from a laptop to production in minutes, whether that’s a web application, an autonomous agent, or an MCP server.
Developers reach that platform through several surfaces — native Mac and Windows desktop apps, web-based tooling, and programmatic MCP interfaces — each built and owned by strong, independent engineering teams.

This role sits inside that team, bringing coherence across the desktop, web, and MCP surfaces without slowing down the engineers who already own each one.
Our vision is to innovate and engineer breakthrough digital products to power business performance and transform global health. We do this through our culture of agile, fast-adapting and pioneer working.

What You Will Achieve
We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Developer Surfaces Lead who will be accountable for the technical direction, architecture, and delivery of Spark Pro’s developer surfaces — desktop, web, and MCP.

In this technical leadership role, you will act as the executor and the visionary behind the surfaces’ technical direction. Rather than leading a single team, you will lead through influence across the experienced engineers who already own each surface, reconciling differing approaches into one coherent direction and ensuring a successful delivery of high-quality developer experiences from inception to completion. This role requires exceptional technical knowledge, hands-on credibility in the Electron and Vue desktop codebase, and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams while sharing responsibility with the engineers driving each surface.
You will also be accountable for delivery of security-and privacy-first capabilities while creating an environment where engineers can do their best work as measured by a quarterly Developer’s Experience survey, and alignment and contribution to the service network and technical engineering standards.

A normal work week consists of leading one or more teams of engineers to deliver and implement technical solutions, following your design approach to meet your assigned program objectives and KPIs. You will also collaborate closely and often with your program lead, Digital Lead, and Product Owners, to ensure that technical decisions and their implementation align with broader strategic priorities.

You represent engineering in program and stakeholder meetings, as such you’ll need to be able to think on your feet: provide consultation, identify risks based on a variety of factors, and rely on your past experiences to identify potential solutions and develop ballpark estimates

- Deep understanding of information security regulations, including (not limited to): Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA), Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS), National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), Personally Identifiable Information (PII), and Protected Health Information (PHI), and various other laws and regulations
